question.title: What will be the closing price of Bitcoin (BTC) on October 30, 2026?
question.description:
Bitcoin (BTC) is the largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization. After reaching an all-time high of roughly $126,000 in early October 2025, BTC has traded well below that peak through 2026. In mid-October 2026 it has been range-bound in the low-$80,000s: daily closes (Yahoo Finance BTC-USD) were about $83,115 on Oct 14, $81,604 on Oct 15, and $81,082 on Oct 16, 2026 — roughly 35% below the ATH. A hotter-than-expected US inflation print in mid-October 2026 contributed to a day of large liquidations, and implied volatility has remained elevated (Bitcoin Volatility Index above 40%). Short-term directional model projections (e.g., midforex, Binance) cluster in the $79,000–$83,000 range for late October 2026, but such forecasts are only indicative. Bitcoin trades 24/7, so a "daily close" is a convention; Yahoo Finance and CoinGecko both anchor the daily close to 00:00 UTC.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the daily closing price of Bitcoin (BTC-USD) for October 30, 2026, in US dollars, as reported on the [Yahoo Finance BTC-USD historical data page](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BTC-USD/history/). The resolution value is the number shown in the "Close" column for the row dated Oct 30, 2026 (Yahoo's daily close is anchored to 00:00 UTC). For example, a close of $85,432.10 resolves as 85432.1.
question.fine_print: If the Yahoo Finance BTC-USD historical page is unavailable or does not report a value for October 30, 2026, the daily closing price for that date from [CoinGecko's Bitcoin historical data page](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin/historical_data) will be used instead. If neither source reports a value, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the BTC/USD closing price for October 30, 2026 will be used.
